answer: Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the copper schedule in the orchard ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the raven checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 189 aliases as a result means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest agents do not face at scale. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 3 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 22 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
